commit_message:
[heap] Grow new space lazily to target capacity

So far SemiSpaceNewSpace was always eagerly allocating pages to reach
its target capacity (for both semi spaces). This CL relaxes this
and allocates pages lazily when they are needed for allocation.

This improves bomb-workers by about 0.8%.

findings.title: Missing capacity guard before AllocateOnNewPageBeyondCapacity call
findings.message: After the lazy new-space page allocation was introduced, `SemiSpaceNewSpaceAllocatorPolicy::EnsureAllocation()` can reach the `AllocateOnNewPageBeyondCapacity()` call even when `to_space_` has not yet grown to its `target_capacity_`. `AllocateOnNewPageBeyondCapacity()` contains two DCHECKs that assume the space is already full: `DCHECK_LT(Available(), size_in_bytes)` and `DCHECK(!AddFreshPage())`. When allocation fails due to OOM or virtual-memory exhaustion before the space reaches its target capacity, `Available()` returns `target_capacity_` (because `Capacity() = max(current_capacity_, target_capacity_) = target_capacity_` while `Size() ≈ 0`), which is far larger than `size_in_bytes`, causing the first DCHECK to fire.

related_locations.description: DCHECK_LT(Available(), size_in_bytes) — the DCHECK that fires when the space has not reached target capacity
Capacity() returns max(current_capacity_, target_capacity_), so Available() equals full target_capacity_ when no pages have been lazily allocated yet

findings.suggestion: Before deciding to call ShouldExpandYoungGenerationOnSlowAllocation() (and subsequently AllocateOnNewPageBeyondCapacity()), check whether the space has actually reached its target capacity. If it has not, bail out early and return false, because the failure was caused by an OOM/virtual-memory shortage, not by the space simply being full. The fix adds a ReachedTargetCapacity() predicate (to_space_.current_capacity_ >= target_capacity_) and gates the expansion path on it.

ground_truth.root_cause: The lazy page allocation feature removed the invariant that 'allocation failure ⇒ space is at target capacity.' The `EnsureAllocation()` function on the slow path did not add a guard to verify `to_space_.current_capacity_ >= target_capacity_` before entering the beyond-capacity code path. As a result, `AllocateOnNewPageBeyondCapacity()` is reached in states it was never designed to handle, where `Available()` equals the full target capacity rather than a value smaller than the requested allocation size.
